asked: Evan: learn the process, not dress Meshy's mesh. Coordinator brief: head close-up fit, brute 2 from brute 1's learned settings with a carry-over table, picture-only guess vs fit; score silhouette IoU against Meshy from front, three-quarter, side and back with shots every step.

method.body_fit: fit_to_meshy.py body mode: 19 named knobs (bone scales, MakeHuman muscle/shape weights incl. paired left/right arm muscles, pose degrees), coordinate descent, mean IoU over front, three-quarter, side and back; a screenshot per kept step in steps_body/.
method.head_fit: fit_to_meshy.py head mode: 10 new signed head knobs (bruiser_lib.HEAD_KNOBS: width, depth, height, square, jaw_width, jaw_forward, chin_height, brow_forward, forehead_forward, head_forward) plus head scale, scored on close-ups of the top 17% of the body from front, three-quarter and side; steps in steps_head/.
method.picture_only_guess: A separate agent that never saw brute 2's 3D or fitted values estimated his settings by eye from his picture, given brute 1's picture and fitted card (brute2/character.eye_guess.json, reasons in eye_guess_notes). Built and scored without any fitting.
method.carryover_only: Brute 1's final settings built unchanged and scored against brute 2's Meshy model (brute2/carryover_only/).

findings: Head: the slab head is now reachable with named knobs: brute 1 head IoU 0.923 -> 0.947 (front 0.97, three-quarter 0.96, side 0.91). The silhouette can't see the brow ridge or eye line, so brow/forehead knobs swing between brutes (brute 1 -1.25, brute 2 +1.25): they are not identified by silhouettes and need a shading or depth cue.
Brute 1 body: 0.823 -> 0.844 over four views (three-quarter 0.798 -> 0.835 once it was scored).

Brute 2: brute 1's settings unchanged already score 0.737 body / 0.814 head; fitting raises that to 0.762 / 0.898. 14 of 29 settings carried over within 10%; the body proportions (neck, legs, shins, arm muscles, forearm length) mostly carried, the head and chest depth moved most.

Picture-only guess scored 0.718 body / 0.801 head, below simply reusing brute 1's settings (0.737 / 0.814). The guess was furthest off on chest depth (front picture shows no depth), forearm muscle and elbow bend.

Brute 2's ceiling is structural, not tuning: his fists are closed and ours are open hands (MPFB pose), and his deltoids are round caps the shoulder-muscle target can't make; the three-quarter score drops during the body fit because the knobs trade it against front/back.

Meshy vs the actual picture: 0.961 (brute 1, best at a 23 degree turn) and 0.951 (brute 2, 9 degrees). Brute 1's reference is a three-quarter view, not front; the round-1 fitter never scored against the picture itself (round-1 recipe vs picture: 0.827). Visible misses vs the picture: forearms too thin, hands too long and low, feet too close together.

models_for_scoring.convention: Blender axes: centred in x/y, feet at z=0, facing -Y; glTF on disk is Y-up as usual
